cards.subject: Vector graphics
says: describes an image as mathematical paths and shapes
scales to any size without losing sharpness
stays small in file size when the artwork is simple
cards.use: need a logo that stays sharp from a favicon to a billboard
not: stores an image as a fixed grid of coloured pixels

cards.subject: Raster graphics
says: stores an image as a grid of pixels
looks soft or blocky when enlarged beyond its resolution
suits photographs with continuous tones
cards.use: work with a photograph that needs retouching
not: scales to any size without any loss of quality

cards.subject: Resolution
says: is the amount of pixel detail in a raster image, such as its width and height in pixels
limits how large a raster image can be shown before it looks soft
cards.use: need to know whether a photo is big enough for its intended size

cards.subject: PPI
says: measures how many image pixels fall in one inch of a screen or print
combines with pixel dimensions to give an image's physical size
cards.use: want to relate pixel dimensions to a physical size
not: counts the ink dots a printer lays down per inch

cards.subject: DPI
says: counts printer dots per inch of output
describes the output device rather than the pixels stored in the image file
cards.use: are talking about the dot density of a printer
not: is the number of pixels stored in the image file

cards.subject: A Bezier curve
says: is defined by anchor points and control handles
gives vector shapes their smooth curves
cards.use: need a smooth, editable curve in a vector shape

cards.subject: An anchor point
says: marks a point on a vector path where the path can change direction
carries handles that shape the curve on either side of it
cards.use: want to reshape one corner of a vector path

cards.subject: A stroke
says: is the outline drawn along the edge of a vector path
has a width, cap and join that can be set
cards.use: need an outline around a shape
not: is the colour that floods the inside of a closed shape

cards.subject: A fill
says: is the colour, gradient or pattern inside a closed vector shape
can be set independently of the outline
cards.use: need a shape to be solid or gradient-coloured inside
not: is the line drawn along the edge of a path

cards.subject: Rasterising
says: converts vector artwork into a pixel image at a chosen size
cannot be reversed to recover the original paths exactly
cards.use: must turn vector artwork into pixels for a fixed-size output

cards.subject: Auto-tracing
says: converts a raster image into vector paths automatically
often leaves extra anchor points that need manual clean-up
cards.use: are handed a low-resolution logo and need a vector version

cards.subject: A layer
says: stacks one piece of artwork above or below others
can be hidden, locked or reordered without altering the others
cards.use: need to edit the background without disturbing the text

cards.subject: A group
says: bundles selected objects so they move and transform together
keeps its contents individually editable when opened
cards.use: want several objects to move as one unit

cards.subject: An artboard
says: is a separate canvas inside one file, such as one page or screen size
lets several sizes of one design sit side by side
can be exported on its own
cards.use: need the same design at several sizes in one file

cards.subject: A frame
says: is a container that can clip its contents to its edges
can carry layout rules such as constraints or auto layout
cards.use: need a screen or card container that clips and arranges its content

cards.subject: A component
says: is a reusable element defined once
holds the master definition that its copies follow
cards.use: want a button designed once and reused everywhere

cards.subject: An instance
says: is a linked copy of a component
inherits changes made to its main component
can override chosen properties such as its text
cards.use: place a copy of a button on a screen and relabel it
not: is the master definition that edits are made in

cards.subject: A variant
says: is one state or option of a component, such as hover or disabled
groups related versions of a component into one set
cards.use: need one component to cover sizes and states

cards.subject: A layer mask
says: uses black and white values to hide and reveal pixels non-destructively
can be repainted to bring hidden content back
cards.use: want to hide part of a photo without erasing it
not: limits visibility to the outline of the layer beneath

cards.subject: A clipping mask
says: limits the visibility of a layer to the shape of the layer beneath
lets a photo show only inside a shape
cards.use: want an image to appear only inside a given shape
not: is painted in black and white to hide pixels

cards.subject: A smart object
says: embeds source content so it can be scaled repeatedly without degrading it
can be linked to a separate file so edits update every use
cards.use: expect to resize a placed image several times in a raster editor

cards.subject: An adjustment layer
says: applies tone or colour changes without altering the pixels beneath
can be switched off or edited later
cards.use: want to change a photo's brightness while keeping the original untouched

cards.subject: Auto layout
says: resizes and spaces a container based on its contents
stacks children with set direction, spacing and padding
cards.use: need a button that grows with its label

cards.subject: A constraint
says: pins an object to an edge or the centre of its parent frame
decides how an object responds when the parent is resized
cards.use: need a logo to stay at the top right when a frame is resized

cards.subject: SVG
says: is a text-based XML vector format
can be edited in a text editor
is embedded directly in web pages and styled with CSS
cards.use: need a crisp logo or icon on a web page
not: stores a fixed grid of pixels

cards.subject: PNG
says: uses lossless compression
supports transparency through an alpha channel
suits screenshots and flat graphics as a raster
cards.use: need a transparent raster image with sharp edges
not: discards detail to shrink the file

cards.subject: JPEG
says: uses lossy compression
suits photographs
has no transparency support
cards.use: are publishing a photograph where a small file matters
not: supports transparency through an alpha channel

cards.subject: WebP
says: supports both lossy and lossless compression
supports transparency and animation
was designed for use on the web
cards.use: want one web image format that covers photographs and transparent graphics

cards.subject: AVIF
says: compresses with an image codec derived from a video codec
supports transparency and wide colour gamut
cards.use: want very efficient web photography and accept less universal tool support

cards.subject: GIF
says: is limited to a palette of 256 colours per frame
supports simple frame-by-frame animation
cards.use: need a very simple looping animation that works anywhere

cards.subject: PDF
says: preserves layout, fonts and graphics in a fixed-page document
can hold both vector and raster content
cards.use: need to send a fixed-layout or print-ready document
not: can only contain text and no images

cards.subject: An AI file
says: is Adobe Illustrator's native editable vector format
keeps artboards, layers and live effects editable
cards.use: need the editable master of a vector logo

cards.subject: A PSD file
says: is Photoshop's native layered raster format
keeps layers, masks and adjustment layers editable
cards.use: need the editable master of a retouched image

cards.subject: EPS
says: is an older PostScript-based format used for vector artwork
does not support transparency natively
cards.use: are asked by a printer for a legacy vector format

cards.subject: TIFF
says: is a flexible raster format common in print and scanning
can hold CMYK data and lossless compression
cards.use: need a high-quality raster master for a print workflow

cards.subject: A camera RAW file
says: stores unprocessed sensor data
must be developed before it is shared
cards.use: need maximum latitude to correct exposure after a shoot
not: is a compressed web-ready photograph

cards.subject: RGB
says: mixes red, green and blue light additively
is the colour model used by screens
reaches white when all channels are at full strength
cards.use: are designing for a screen
not: mixes inks subtractively

cards.subject: CMYK
says: mixes cyan, magenta, yellow and black inks subtractively
is the model behind process-colour printing
usually reproduces fewer saturated colours than a screen
cards.use: are preparing artwork for four-colour printing
not: mixes light additively

cards.subject: A gamut
says: is the range of colours a device or colour space can reproduce
differs between a screen and a printing process
cards.use: ask why a bright screen colour cannot be printed

cards.subject: An ICC profile
says: describes how a device's colour values map to real colours
can be embedded in a file to keep colour consistent between devices
cards.use: need colour to look the same on different devices

cards.subject: sRGB
says: is the standard default RGB colour space for the web
is the safe choice when the viewing device is unknown
cards.use: are exporting images for general web viewing

cards.subject: A wide-gamut colour space
says: covers a wider range of colours than sRGB
needs a colour-managed workflow to display as intended
cards.use: work on screens and images that exceed sRGB

cards.subject: A spot colour
says: is a premixed ink printed on its own plate
is specified by name from a matching library
cards.use: need a brand colour reproduced exactly by a premixed ink
not: is built from halftone dots of the four process inks

cards.subject: A hex colour code
says: writes an RGB colour as six hexadecimal digits
is the usual way to specify a screen colour in CSS
cards.use: need to hand a developer an exact screen colour

cards.subject: HSL
says: describes colour by hue, saturation and lightness
makes light and dark variants of one hue easy to create
cards.use: want to derive tints and shades of a single hue

cards.subject: Colour management
says: converts colour values between profiles so appearance stays consistent
relies on every stage knowing the profile of the file
cards.use: see colours shift between design software and the browser

cards.subject: A rendering intent
says: chooses how out-of-gamut colours are mapped during a profile conversion
includes options such as perceptual and relative colorimetric
cards.use: convert a vivid image to a smaller gamut and want to control the result

cards.subject: RGB-to-CMYK conversion
says: can dull saturated colours that fall outside the CMYK gamut
is best done late, from the RGB master, using the target profile
cards.use: must prepare an RGB design for print

cards.subject: An alpha channel
says: stores per-pixel transparency
lets an image blend onto any background
cards.use: need a logo that sits over different backgrounds

cards.subject: Bit depth
says: sets how many tonal levels each colour channel can hold
reduces visible banding in gradients when it is higher
cards.use: see stepped bands in a smooth gradient

cards.subject: Lossy compression
says: discards some image data to shrink the file
cannot restore the discarded detail afterwards
cards.use: need the smallest file for a photograph and can accept minor loss

cards.subject: Lossless compression
says: shrinks a file while allowing exact reconstruction of the original pixels
gives smaller savings on photographs than lossy compression
cards.use: must keep every pixel exactly as designed

cards.subject: Exporting at 2x
says: produces an image with twice the pixel dimensions of its layout size
keeps images sharp on high-density screens
cards.use: need an icon to look sharp on a high-density display

cards.subject: Slicing
says: marks a region of a design to be exported as its own image
lets one artboard produce several separate files
cards.use: need several images cut from one composed layout

cards.subject: SVG optimisation
says: removes editor metadata and redundant markup from an SVG
keeps the visual result unchanged
cards.use: find an exported SVG is full of editor-specific data

cards.subject: A responsive image
says: offers the browser several sizes of one image to choose from
avoids sending phones an image sized for a large monitor
cards.use: serve one photo to phones and large desktops efficiently

cards.subject: Stripping metadata
says: removes EXIF and editor data from an exported file
can remove location data embedded in photographs
cards.use: publish a photograph that may carry the camera's location

cards.subject: Resizing before export
says: avoids shipping more pixels than the layout displays
is done to the largest size the image will be shown at
cards.use: find a hero photo several times larger than it is displayed

cards.subject: Choosing a JPEG quality level
says: trades file size against visible artefacts
is judged by eye on the actual image because results vary with content
cards.use: need to pick a compression setting for a photograph

cards.subject: Lazy loading
says: delays loading offscreen images until the visitor scrolls near them
reduces the data fetched on first view of a page
cards.use: want long pages with many images to load quickly at first

cards.subject: An SVG sprite
says: bundles many icons into one file referenced by id
lets one request serve a whole icon set
cards.use: want an icon set delivered in a single file

cards.subject: A progressive JPEG
says: loads as a blurry full image that sharpens in passes
shows the whole picture early on slow connections
cards.use: want a large photo to show something quickly on a slow connection

cards.subject: Dithering
says: simulates missing colours by patterning pixels in a limited palette
can make a gradient look smoother in a 256-colour image
cards.use: must reduce a gradient to a small palette without harsh banding

cards.subject: A wireframe
says: sketches structure and layout without final visual styling
focuses on placement and function rather than colour and imagery
cards.use: want to agree page structure before spending time on visuals
not: is a fully styled picture of the finished screen

cards.subject: A mockup
says: shows a static, visually styled version of a design
has no working interactions
cards.use: need stakeholders to see exactly how a screen will look
not: responds to clicks like the finished product

cards.subject: A prototype
says: simulates how a design behaves through clickable interactions
can be tested with users before any code is written
cards.use: want users to try a flow before it is built
not: is the finished product released to customers

cards.subject: A low-fidelity prototype
says: is a rough, quick version such as paper sketches or grey boxes
invites feedback on structure rather than polish
cards.use: need quick feedback on an idea before investing in detail

cards.subject: A high-fidelity prototype
says: closely resembles the final look and behaviour
suits testing visual hierarchy and microinteractions
takes longer to build and change
cards.use: need to test details of the look and feel with users

cards.subject: A user flow
says: maps the steps a person takes to complete a task
shows screens and decision points along a path
cards.use: want to map how someone moves from start to goal

cards.subject: A trigger
says: defines the click, tap or hover that starts a prototype action
connects one frame to another
cards.use: need a button to take the viewer to the next screen

cards.subject: A prototype transition
says: defines the animation between two prototype states
can be a dissolve, a slide or a push
cards.use: want the move between two screens to feel animated

cards.subject: A usability test
says: observes real users attempting tasks with a prototype
uncovers confusion the design team can no longer see
cards.use: want evidence of where users get stuck

cards.subject: A design system
says: collects reusable components, styles and guidance in one source
helps separate teams build screens that look consistent
cards.use: need many designers and developers to produce consistent interfaces

cards.subject: A microinteraction
says: is a small animated response to a single action, such as a toggle moving
gives feedback that an action registered
cards.use: want a switch to acknowledge a tap

cards.subject: A coded prototype
says: uses real code to test behaviour a design tool cannot simulate
can use real data and measure speed
cards.use: must test performance or real data that a mock cannot show

cards.subject: Inspect mode
says: shows measurements, colours and code snippets for selected elements
lets developers read values straight from the design
cards.use: are a developer who needs exact spacing and colour from a design

cards.subject: A redline
says: annotates a design with spacing, size and alignment measurements
goes stale when the design changes after it is drawn
cards.use: must communicate exact spacing in a static handoff

cards.subject: A design token
says: stores a design decision such as colour, spacing or type size as a named value
lets one change propagate to both design and code
cards.use: want a colour change to flow through every screen and codebase

cards.subject: A spacing scale
says: limits spacing to a small set of agreed values
removes one-off gaps that nobody can justify
cards.use: find spacing differs slightly on every screen

cards.subject: Marking assets for export
says: tells developers which layers to export and in which formats and scales
avoids developers guessing what to extract
cards.use: want developers to pull the right icon files themselves

cards.subject: Documenting component states
says: lists how an element looks when hovered, focused, disabled or in error
prevents developers from inventing missing states
cards.use: need to list the hover, focus and disabled looks of a button for developers

cards.subject: Design-to-code parity
says: keeps design components and coded components alike in name and behaviour
reduces rework when the two drift apart
cards.use: find the design library and the code library have different names for the same button

cards.subject: Linking the design file from the requirement
says: lets readers find the mockup next to what it must satisfy
is most useful with a note of the decision the prototype supported
cards.use: want a requirement and its design to stay connected

cards.subject: A handoff walkthrough
says: lets the designer explain intent before building starts
surfaces developer questions early
cards.use: want to avoid misreadings of a complex design

cards.subject: An accessibility annotation
says: specifies reading order, focus order, labels and alt text for developers
records a need that a visual comp cannot show
cards.use: must tell developers how a screen should work with a screen reader

cards.subject: Design QA
says: compares the built result against the design before release
catches drift in spacing, colour and states
cards.use: want to check that what was built matches what was designed

cards.subject: A naming convention
says: gives files predictable names with agreed order, case and separators
makes assets findable by search and sort
cards.use: find files called final, final2 and final_new in one folder

cards.subject: A master file
says: is the editable original from which every export is made
should be kept even when only exports are shared
cards.use: need to change a logo after it has been sent out in several formats
not: is a flattened copy made for one use

cards.subject: A derivative file
says: is a flattened or converted copy made for a particular use
should be regenerated from the master rather than edited
cards.use: need a web copy of an approved print logo
not: is the editable original of the artwork

cards.subject: A digital asset management system
says: stores approved assets with metadata, search and permissions in one place
tracks usage so copies do not drift across drives and email
cards.use: have approved brand files scattered across drives and inboxes

cards.subject: Asset metadata
says: describes a file with tags, keywords, usage rights and authorship
makes assets searchable beyond their filenames
cards.use: cannot find an image because its filename says nothing

cards.subject: A licence record
says: records where an image or font came from and what use it permits
stops unlicensed material entering a campaign
cards.use: must prove that a stock image may be used in a client campaign

cards.subject: A brand asset library
says: collects approved logos, icons and templates for everyday use
gives staff one place to fetch the current version
cards.use: want staff to stop using outdated logos

cards.subject: Packaging a file
says: gathers a file with its linked images and fonts into one folder
lets another person open the work with nothing missing
cards.use: need to send a layout to a printer who lacks your fonts

cards.subject: A linked image
says: stays a separate file referenced by the design
breaks when the design is moved without it
cards.use: see a missing-links warning after moving a project folder
not: is stored inside the design file itself

cards.subject: An embedded image
says: is stored inside the design file
enlarges the file but travels with it
cards.use: want a design file that cannot lose its pictures
not: stays a separate file referenced by the design

cards.subject: A single approved version
says: marks one file as the current approved artwork
removes doubt about which logo file to use
cards.use: find three near-identical logo files in circulation

cards.subject: Archiving a project
says: moves finished work to long-term storage with masters, fonts and links together
keeps the work reopenable years later
cards.use: are closing a finished project and want to reopen it later

cards.subject: A font family
says: groups related weights and styles of one typeface
includes variants such as regular, italic and bold
cards.use: need a consistent set of weights for a brand

cards.subject: A variable font
says: holds a range of weights or widths in one file
allows continuous adjustment between its extremes
cards.use: want many weights without many separate files

cards.subject: Kerning
says: adjusts the space between a specific pair of letters
fixes awkward gaps such as in AV
cards.use: see an uneven gap between two particular letters

cards.subject: Tracking
says: adjusts the spacing across a whole run of text evenly
is often opened up slightly for small capitals
cards.use: want to loosen a whole line of text

cards.subject: Leading
says: is the vertical distance between lines of text
makes paragraphs feel tight or airy
cards.use: find lines of body text too cramped

cards.subject: Font embedding
says: stores the font inside a PDF so it displays correctly everywhere
is subject to the font's licence terms
cards.use: must send a PDF to a reader who lacks the typeface

cards.subject: A webfont
says: is a font file served to the browser with a page
lets a site use a typeface the visitor does not have installed
cards.use: want a page to show the brand typeface on any device

cards.subject: A fallback font
says: is a substitute used when the first-choice font is unavailable
is listed after the preferred font in a font stack
cards.use: want text to remain legible if the brand font fails to load

cards.subject: A type scale
says: is a set of related text sizes with a consistent ratio
keeps headings and body text in proportion
cards.use: find text sizes chosen arbitrarily on each screen

cards.subject: A font licence
says: states how a typeface may be installed, embedded and distributed
can differ for print, web and app use
cards.use: want to put a purchased font on a website

cards.subject: Bleed
says: extends artwork beyond the trim edge
prevents white slivers when the page is cut
cards.use: have a background colour that runs to the edge of a printed page

cards.subject: A crop mark
says: shows the printer where to cut
sits outside the trim area
cards.use: need to show the printer where the sheet is trimmed

cards.subject: A safe margin
says: keeps text and logos clear of the trim edge
protects content from slight cutting variation
cards.use: want text not to be cut off by trimming

cards.subject: Print resolution
says: is commonly about 300 pixels per inch at final size for photographs
falls short when a small web image is stretched to poster size
cards.use: must decide whether a photo is big enough for a printed leaflet

cards.subject: Overprint
says: prints one ink over another instead of knocking out what lies beneath
can cause unexpected colours when set by accident
cards.use: see a colour mixing with the one underneath in a proof

cards.subject: Rich black
says: mixes CMYK inks to print a deeper black than black ink alone
is suited to large solid areas rather than small text
cards.use: want a large black background to look deep and solid

cards.subject: Transparency flattening
says: merges overlapping transparent objects into opaque output
is needed by older output workflows
cards.use: must output transparency to a workflow that cannot handle it

cards.subject: Preflight
says: checks a file for print problems such as missing fonts and low-resolution images
is run before artwork goes to the printer
cards.use: want to catch print problems before the file leaves

cards.subject: PDF/X
says: is a family of PDF standards restricting content for reliable print exchange
typically requires fonts embedded and defined colour handling
cards.use: need a print PDF that meets a printer's standard

cards.subject: Converting text to outlines
says: turns live text into vector shapes so no font is needed
makes the text no longer editable as text
cards.use: must send artwork to a printer who lacks the typeface

cards.subject: A proof
says: shows how the job will look before the full run is printed
may be a soft proof on screen or a hard copy on paper
cards.use: want to approve colour before a large print run

cards.subject: Trapping
says: slightly overlaps adjoining colours to hide gaps from misregistration
is applied where plates may not line up perfectly
cards.use: fear thin white gaps where two printed colours meet

cards.subject: Total ink coverage
says: caps the combined ink percentage of CMYK in the darkest areas
prevents wet or smudging ink on press
cards.use: find a dark area too saturated with ink for the press

cards.subject: Responsive design
says: adapts a layout to the width of the viewing screen
lets one design serve phones, tablets and desktops
cards.use: want one page to work on phones and desktops

cards.subject: A breakpoint
says: is a width at which a layout changes
is where columns reflow or navigation changes form
cards.use: need the navigation to change on narrow screens

cards.subject: Device pixel ratio
says: is the number of physical pixels per CSS pixel
is why 2x assets look sharp on dense screens
cards.use: ask why images look soft on a phone but sharp on an older monitor

cards.subject: A layout grid
says: divides a frame into columns with gutters and margins
helps elements align across screens
cards.use: want elements to line up consistently across pages

cards.subject: A contrast ratio
says: compares the luminance of text and its background
is what accessibility guidelines use to judge legibility
cards.use: need to check that grey text is readable on white

cards.subject: Alt text
says: describes an image's content or purpose for people who cannot see it
is left empty for purely decorative images
cards.use: add a photograph to a web page for screen reader users

cards.subject: A favicon
says: is the small icon shown in browser tabs and bookmarks
must stay recognisable at very small sizes
cards.use: want a brand mark visible in a browser tab

cards.subject: A dark colour scheme
says: needs its own chosen colour pairs rather than a simple inversion
must still meet contrast requirements
cards.use: are adding a dark theme to an interface

cards.subject: An icon grid
says: keeps icons the same overall size and optical weight
provides keylines for circles, squares and rectangles
cards.use: find icons in one set look uneven next to each other

cards.subject: Colour-independent cues
says: convey meaning through text, shape or icon as well as colour
help people with colour vision deficiency
cards.use: mark an error state in a form

cards.subject: GuruGraphics
says: is a UK brand identity studio
does design and branding only
does not sell software, development, hosting or support
cards.use: are asked whether this studio builds websites or hosting

cards.subject: Brand Discovery master artwork
says: is supplied in AI, PDF, SVG, JPG and PNG
comes from the first engagement
cards.use: want to know which file formats the first engagement delivers

cards.subject: The editable working file set
says: is handed over first in the Identity Programme
lets the client's own team adjust artwork later
cards.use: want to know when the studio hands over editable source files

cards.subject: A digital asset library
says: gathers approved brand assets in digital form
is meant for the client to reuse in daily work
cards.use: want to name the deliverable that gathers approved brand assets for reuse

cards.subject: A favicon and channel icon set
says: serves small digital placements such as browser tabs and channels
has to stay recognisable when shown very small
cards.use: want to name the deliverable for tab and channel branding

cards.subject: The Brand System guidelines document
says: runs to 30-60 pages
covers logo, colour and typography rules
includes accessibility and contrast standards
cards.use: want to know what the guidelines contain

cards.subject: Governance and asset management setup
says: is first included in the Rollout Programme
helps a client keep rolled-out assets consistent
cards.use: want to know which engagement sets up asset governance

cards.subject: The Brand Applications step
says: translates the identity into real touchpoints
spans signage and stationery as well as digital media and presentations
cards.use: want to know which step turns an identity into real-world items

cards.subject: The Brand Launch step
says: equips teams with the creative assets and direction to introduce the identity
comes last of the five steps
cards.use: want to know which step prepares a team to launch a new identity

qa.q: A client's logo must appear on a business card, a website favicon and a roadside billboard. Which master format is the safest starting point?
qa.right: A vector file such as SVG or AI
qa.why: Vector artwork scales to any size without losing sharpness.

qa.q: You enlarge a 200-pixel-wide photograph to fill a poster and it looks soft and blocky. What is the cause?
qa.right: The raster image does not hold enough pixel detail for the larger size
wrong: The file is in RGB instead of CMYK
The image has too many layers
The file needs a different colour profile
qa.why: Raster images are limited by their resolution.

qa.q: Which file would you choose for a photograph on a web page where file size matters most and transparency is not needed?
qa.right: JPEG
qa.why: JPEG's lossy compression suits photographs.

qa.q: Which format suits a flat logo that needs a transparent background on a web page and must stay sharp at any size?
qa.right: SVG
qa.why: SVG is a vector format that supports transparency.

qa.q: A designer re-saves the same JPEG five times, each time applying compression. What is the effect?
qa.right: Quality degrades cumulatively because each save discards more data
qa.why: Lossy compression cannot restore discarded data and repeats compound loss.

qa.q: A screen design in RGB is going to a commercial printer. What should you do?
qa.right: Convert from the RGB master to the printer's CMYK profile and check the colours that shift
wrong: Send the RGB file unchanged and trust the press to match
Flatten the file to a GIF
qa.why: Out-of-gamut colours can dull, so convert deliberately and review.

qa.q: A printed leaflet has thin white slivers along the edge where the background colour should run to the paper edge. What was probably missing?
qa.right: Bleed beyond the trim edge
qa.why: Bleed extends artwork past the cut line so trimming variation does not show white.

qa.q: A printer opens your layout and reports missing fonts. Which is the best remedy?
qa.right: Package the file with its fonts and links, or outline the text if licences allow
wrong: Convert the layout to a GIF
qa.why: The printer needs the fonts or text as outlines.

qa.q: What is the difference between a clipping mask and a layer mask?
qa.right: A clipping mask uses the shape of the layer beneath, while a layer mask uses black and white to hide and reveal pixels
wrong: A clipping mask deletes pixels, while a layer mask is a fill colour
They are two names for the same feature
A clipping mask applies only to text
qa.why: They hide content in different ways.

qa.q: Why do instances of a component update when the main component is edited?
qa.right: Instances are linked to the main component and inherit its changes
wrong: Each instance has its own copy of the master
qa.why: Linked instances follow their master except for overrides.

qa.q: A designer changes the label on one button instance. What happens to the main component?
qa.right: Nothing, because a text override applies to that instance only
wrong: The instance becomes detached automatically and deleted
qa.why: Overrides are local to the instance.

qa.q: Which statement about PNG and JPEG is correct?
qa.right: PNG is lossless and supports transparency, while JPEG is lossy and does not
wrong: JPEG is lossless and supports transparency
PNG always produces smaller files for photographs
qa.why: These are the standard properties of the formats.

qa.q: Which pair describes GIF correctly?
qa.right: A palette of up to 256 colours per frame and simple animation
qa.why: GIF is palette-limited.

qa.q: Which is a good reason to export an icon at 2x?
qa.right: High-density screens have more physical pixels per layout pixel, so a 1x image looks soft
wrong: It converts the icon to vector
qa.why: 2x assets match dense screens.

qa.q: A web page serves a 4000-pixel photograph that is displayed 800 pixels wide. What is the best fix?
qa.right: Resize and compress for the display size, ideally offering multiple sizes with responsive images
wrong: Convert the photograph to a GIF
Embed it as base64 in the page
Leave it, since browsers shrink it for free
qa.why: The browser still downloads every pixel.

qa.q: Exported SVGs from your design tool are full of editor-specific metadata. What should you do?
qa.right: Run an SVG optimiser to strip redundant markup while keeping the visual result
wrong: Open them in a text editor and delete everything
qa.why: Optimisation removes unneeded data.

qa.q: What does a prototype have that a mockup does not?
qa.right: Interactions that simulate how the design behaves
qa.why: A mockup is static.

qa.q: A team wants quick feedback on structure for a new checkout idea before investing in detail. Which approach fits best?
qa.right: A low-fidelity prototype or wireframe
qa.why: Low fidelity invites feedback on structure.

qa.q: Why test a prototype with real users instead of only reviewing it internally?
qa.right: Users reveal confusion that the team can no longer see
wrong: It removes the need for requirements
qa.why: Teams are too close to their own design.

qa.q: A team needs to know whether a screen feels fast with real data. Which tool is most appropriate?
qa.right: A coded prototype
qa.why: A design tool mock cannot show speed or real data.

qa.q: A prototype looks polished and a stakeholder assumes the product is nearly finished. What is the best practice?
qa.right: Label it as a prototype and state what is not real
wrong: Add more polish so it looks finished
qa.why: A polished prototype can be mistaken for a finished product.

qa.q: What is the purpose of design tokens?
qa.right: To store decisions like colour and spacing as named values shared between design and code
qa.why: Tokens centralise design decisions.

qa.q: A developer cannot tell how a button looks when focused or disabled because the design shows only one state. What was missing?
qa.right: Documented component states
qa.why: Handoff should list the states.

qa.q: Why link the design file from the requirement it satisfies?
qa.right: So readers can find the mockup next to what it must satisfy, ideally with a note on the decision it supported
wrong: To remove the need for review
To make the design editable by anyone
qa.why: A design file alone does not record why.

qa.q: A team has three near-identical logo files in circulation and staff keep using the wrong one. Which practice helps most?
qa.right: Mark a single approved version in a shared library or DAM
wrong: Rename the files with the date
Email the logo to everyone again
qa.why: One authoritative approved file removes doubt.

qa.q: What is the difference between a master file and a derivative?
qa.right: The master is the editable original, while a derivative is a copy made for a specific use
wrong: The master is always a JPEG
A derivative is the editable original
qa.why: Exports should be regenerated from the master.

qa.q: A designer moves a project folder and the layout now shows missing links. What most likely happened?
qa.right: Linked images were not moved with the design
wrong: The file was converted to CMYK
qa.why: Linked images are referenced from separate files.

qa.q: Which is true of embedded images?
qa.right: They are stored inside the design file, making it larger but self-contained
wrong: They are separate files that can go missing
qa.why: Embedding trades size for portability.

qa.q: Two designers need to work on the same design and review each other's changes without disturbing the approved main file. Which feature helps?
qa.right: Branching and merging
qa.why: Branches isolate exploratory changes.

qa.q: A reviewer finds a stakeholder's feedback was based on an attached copy that was already out of date. What practice avoids this?
qa.right: Share a link to the live file so reviewers see the latest version
qa.why: Links point to the latest version.

qa.q: You share a design by link set so anyone with the link can open it. What should you check first?
qa.right: That no unreleased work is exposed to unintended viewers
qa.why: Link permissions can expose unreleased work.

qa.q: A shared component library is updated by one designer. How should the team receive the changes?
qa.right: By accepting the published library update in the files that use it
qa.why: Libraries publish updates to consumers.

qa.q: What is the right way to compare ink-based print colour with a screen colour before a big run?
qa.right: Approve a proof from the printer
qa.why: Proofs show how the job will print.

qa.q: What does kerning adjust?
qa.right: The space between a specific pair of letters
wrong: The space between every letter in a line
qa.why: Kerning is pair-specific.

qa.q: What is leading?
qa.right: The vertical distance between lines of text
qa.why: Leading controls line spacing.

qa.q: Why list a fallback font in a font stack?
qa.right: So text stays legible if the preferred font does not load
wrong: So fonts are embedded in PDFs
qa.why: A fallback keeps text readable.

qa.q: You want to put a purchased font on a website. What should you check?
qa.right: That the font licence permits web use
wrong: That the font is in CMYK
qa.why: Licences can differ by use.

qa.q: Large black background areas in a print job look washed out. Which technique helps?
qa.right: Rich black built from several inks
qa.why: Rich black gives a deeper solid.

qa.q: Why use rich black for large areas but usually not for small text?
qa.right: Small text in several inks can show misregistration
wrong: Rich black cannot be printed small
Black ink is invalid for text
qa.why: Several plates can misalign on fine detail.

qa.q: A designer sets an object to overprint by mistake. What might happen in print?
qa.right: Its ink mixes with the colour beneath instead of knocking it out
qa.why: Overprint prints over the underlying ink.

qa.q: A printer asks for a PDF/X file. What does that mean?
qa.right: A PDF following a standard that restricts content for reliable print exchange
qa.why: PDF/X standardises print PDFs.

qa.q: You are handed a low-resolution raster logo and need a scalable one. What is a typical route?
qa.right: Auto-trace it and clean up the paths, or redraw it
wrong: Enlarge it in a raster editor
Save it as JPEG at higher quality
qa.why: Tracing produces vector paths that need clean-up.

qa.q: A photograph with a smooth sky shows visible stepped bands after processing. Which is the likely cause?
qa.right: Low bit depth or heavy compression
qa.why: Banding appears when tonal levels are limited.

qa.q: A designer inverts a light interface to make a dark theme and some text becomes hard to read. What was the mistake?
qa.right: Inverting instead of choosing dark colour pairs that meet contrast requirements
qa.why: Dark themes need chosen pairs.

qa.q: An error state in a form is shown only by changing the border to red. What should you add?
qa.right: A text message or icon so the meaning does not rely on colour alone
qa.why: Colour alone fails users with colour vision deficiency.

qa.q: A brand has a colour that must match exactly across packaging and signage regardless of press. Which is the best approach?
qa.right: Specify it as a spot colour
wrong: Specify it as an RGB hex code only
qa.why: Spot colours are premixed.

qa.q: Which engagement first delivers master artwork in AI, PDF, SVG, JPG and PNG, according to the studio's offer?
qa.right: Brand Discovery
qa.why: The first engagement includes master artwork in those five formats.

qa.q: A client of GuruGraphics asks the studio to host their website. How should this be answered?
qa.right: The studio does design and branding only and does not sell hosting
wrong: Yes, hosting is included in Brand System
Hosting is included with the logo
qa.why: GuruGraphics does not sell hosting.

qa.q: A client wants editable working files and a digital asset library. Which engagement first includes them?
qa.right: The Identity Programme
qa.why: Both are listed in the Identity Programme.

qa.q: A client wants guidelines that include accessibility and contrast standards. Which engagement provides them?
qa.right: The Brand System
qa.why: The Brand System includes 30-60 page guidelines with accessibility and contrast standards.

qa.q: A client wants a plan to roll a new identity out across estate, signage and print. Which engagement includes it?
qa.right: The Rollout Programme
qa.why: The Rollout Programme includes the estate, signage and print rollout plan.

qa.q: A client asks which engagement sets up governance and asset management. Which is correct?
qa.right: The Rollout Programme
qa.why: Governance and asset management setup is listed in the Rollout Programme.
